source_of_truth: The frozen judge-only reference dossier; candidates answer from internal knowledge.
evaluation_principles: Reward a correct causal chain from mRNA delivery to immune memory.
Require precise correction of DNA and breakthrough-infection misconceptions.
Do not judge individual medical advice because the prompt explicitly excludes it.

key_facts.label: Temporary instructions
key_facts.expected: Vaccine mRNA provides temporary instructions that ribosomes translate into a harmless antigen or antigen fragment.

key_facts.label: Immune response and memory
key_facts.expected: The immune system recognizes the antigen and develops adaptive responses including antibodies and memory.

key_facts.label: No live virus
key_facts.expected: An mRNA vaccine contains no live SARS-CoV-2 and cannot itself cause COVID-19.

key_facts.label: No DNA alteration
key_facts.expected: The mRNA acts in the cytoplasm, does not enter the nucleus or interact with chromosomal DNA, and does not integrate into it.

key_facts.label: mRNA breakdown
key_facts.expected: Cells break down the vaccine mRNA after the instructions have been used.

key_facts.label: Protection is probabilistic
key_facts.expected: Vaccination reduces probabilities and does not guarantee that infection is impossible.

key_facts.label: Different protection endpoints
key_facts.expected: Distinguishes infection, symptoms and severe outcomes, with potentially different effectiveness and waning.

key_facts.label: Breakthrough interpretation
key_facts.expected: Explains why a breakthrough infection is compatible with reduced risk or severity and does not alone demonstrate no effect.

key_ideas.label: Information is not genetic rewriting
key_ideas.expected: Uses the temporary-instruction idea to make clear why antigen production is not permanent modification of DNA.

key_ideas.label: Training rather than force field
key_ideas.expected: Explains that vaccination prepares a faster immune response rather than physically preventing every viral entry.

key_ideas.label: Outcome-specific effectiveness
key_ideas.expected: Shows that effectiveness must be tied to a defined endpoint, especially infection versus severe disease.

key_ideas.label: Risk reduction, not individual guarantee
key_ideas.expected: Communicates probabilistic benefit without overpromising or treating one outcome as proof of population-level ineffectiveness.

known_critical_errors.description: Claims that vaccine mRNA enters the nucleus, integrates into or otherwise rewrites the recipient's DNA.
Claims that an mRNA vaccine contains live SARS-CoV-2 or can cause COVID-19 infection.
Claims that vaccination guarantees infection cannot occur.
Treats any breakthrough infection as proof that vaccination had no effect.
Collapses protection from infection and protection from severe disease into one all-or-nothing outcome.

anchors.25: No material factual or mechanistic error.
anchors.20: Accurate overall with one minor imprecision.
anchors.12: At least one major error or several meaningful imprecisions.

anchors.10: Connects cellular mechanism, immune response and clinical outcomes coherently.
anchors.7: Sound explanation with one underdeveloped connection.
anchors.4: Mostly lists facts without a clear causal chain.

anchors.10: Consistently uses calibrated risk language and distinguishes endpoints.
anchors.7: Mostly precise with one limited ambiguity.

anchors.10: Clear German, descriptive structure and understandable without medical training.

anchors.5: High information density without material repetition.
anchors.0: Exceeds the hard maximum or is not focused.
